title: Visualizing Complex Square Roots and Root-Coefficient Mapping
full_prompt: Write a Manim scene named `StudySqrt` (inheriting from a base `RootCoefScene` or implementing it directly) that visualizes the relationship between complex numbers and their square roots. Create two side-by-side complex planes: one representing the 'Root' plane (or output plane) and the other representing the 'Coefficient' or input plane. Place a dot on the input plane that moves in a continuous circular path around the origin. On the root plane, display the corresponding square roots of this moving value. Because every non-zero complex number has two square roots, show both roots as distinct, color-coded dots. As the input dot completes one full 360-degree rotation, animate the two root dots to show them swapping positions (each completing a 180-degree half-rotation), beautifully illustrating the branch structure and multi-valued nature of the complex square root function. Use continuous tracer lines to show the paths of all dots, and clear text labels to identify the planes and coordinates.

visual_techniques: Optimal transport sorting to prevent discontinuous jumps in root tracking

common_failure_modes.pattern: Discontinuous jumping of root dots due to branch cuts during sorting
common_failure_modes.note: Must use a tracking/sorting algorithm like optimal_transport to pair the closest roots to their previous positions instead of sorting by raw angle.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Mismatched coordinate systems between the two complex planes
common_failure_modes.note: Ensure points are mapped correctly using plane.n2p (number to point) and plane.p2n (point to number).
